title: M/S Hdfc Bnak Ltd vs Manoj Bansal on 14 November, 2011
full_text: M/S Hdfc Bnak Ltd vs Manoj Bansal on 14 November, 2011 IN THE COURT OF SHRI ARUN KUMAR, METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE:DWARKA COURTS:NEW DELHI CC NO: 11607/09 Unique Case ID No: RO001552011 M/s HDFC Bnak Ltd. A Company incorporated under the Companies Act,1956 Having its office at 2nd Floor, Express Building Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg ITO, New Delhi Through its Attorney Gopal Ranga ...............Complainant Versus Manoj Bansal House No. 1302, Ground Floor Kundy­Walan, Ajmeri Gate Near Hanuman Mandir Delhi­110006 ................Accused Offence Complained of or proved : Under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 1 of 21 Plea of the Accused : Pleaded not guilty Date of filing : 01.08.2009 Date of Institution : 17.08.2009 Date of reserving judgment/order : 12.10.2011 Final Order/Judgment : Acquitted Date of pronouncement : 14.11.2011 JUDGMENT: BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE:­ 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present complaint u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act filed by the complainant against the accused. 2. Case of the complainant as per the complaint is that the complainant had financed a loan to the accused under loan agreement number 91354455 (Personal Loan) from the erstwhile Centurion Bank of Punjab which was subsequently merged with the complainant bank and in partial discharge of the above said liability the accused issued a cheque bearing number 729099 of Rs. 13,530/­ dated 23/05/2009 drawn on his banker M/s Punjab National Bank, Asaf Ali Road, Delhi­110002. On presentation by the complainant of the aforesaid cheque on its bankers, HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 2 of 21 the cheque was returned unpaid to the complainant with the remarks "account closed" on 28.05.2009, upon which the complainant issued a demand notice dated 11.06.2009 under Section 138 of the NI Act through registered post dated 15.06.2009 calling upon the accused to make payment in respect of the dishonoured cheque within fifteen days from the receipt of notice. Since the accused had failed to make the payment, the complainant had filed the present complaint under Section 138 of the NI Act against the accused through its duly authorized representative Mr. Gopal Ranga. 3. The accused was summoned vide order dated 17.08.2009, whereupon accused has entered the appearance on 16.03.2010 and was admitted to bail. 4. Notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C. was issued to the accused on 31.05.2010 to which he did not plead guilty and claimed trial and the matter was fixed for complainant's evidence. 5. Complainant has examined Mr. Gopal Ranga, AR of the complainant, as CW­1 in support of submissions made in the complaint. CW­1, adopted his affidavit EX.CW1/A filed by him in pre summoning evidence in his post summoning evidence also and also filed the Loan Agreement Ex. CW­1/X and statement of account of the accused which HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 3 of 21 was marked as Ex. CW­1/Y. Complainant has relied upon the following documents:­ EX.CW1/1: Copy of Power of attorney dated 16.07.2008 in favour of the AR. EX.CW1/2: Original cheque bearing no. 729099 dated 23.05.2009 for a sum of Rs. 13,530/­ drawn on Punjab National Bank, Asaf Ali Road, New Delhi­110002 in favour of M/s Centurion Bank of Punjab. EX.CW1/3: Cheque return memo dated 28.05.2009. EX.CW1/4: Office copy of legal demand notice dated 11.06.2009. EX.CW1/5(Colly): Postal receipt dated 15.06.2009 and AD cards. EX.CW1/X: Copy of Loan Agreement alongwith Sanction Letter Ex. CW1/Y: Statement of Loan account of the accused. 6. CW­1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused and on a separate statement of AR of the complainant, Complainant's evidence was closed vide order dated 29.07.2011. Thereafter, accused was examined u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. on 10.08.2011 and the matter was adjourned for defence evidence. 7. Accused has examined himself as DW­1 after seeking permission of the court under Section 315 of the Cr.P.C. Thereafter, on a separate statement of the accused, the defence evidence was closed vide order HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 4 of 21 dated 26.09.2011 and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 8.Final Arguments in the case were heard on 12.10.2011. Ld. Counsel for the complainant has also filed written submissions. It has been contended by Ld. Counsel for the Complainant that the complainant bank has proved beyond reasonable doubts that the accused had availed a loan of Rs. 1,58,000/­ approx. from the erstwhile Centurion Bank of Punjab in the year 2007, which was repayable by him in 60 EMIs of Rs. 4,510/­ each and in partial discharge of his liability towards the aforesaid loan, the accused had issued the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 in favour of Centurion Bank of Punjab, which, on presentation, was dishonoured since the accused had already closed the account on which the aforesaid cheque had been drawn by him. According to Ld. Counsel for the complainant, since the erstwhile Centurion Bank of Punjab had already been merged with the complainant bank on 20.05.2008 as per the RBI guidelines, the complainant bank had become a holder in due course of the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 and as such when, on presentation, the cheque was dishonoured, a demand notice was served on the accused in terms of Section 138 of the NI Act calling upon him to make the payment within 15 days of the service of the notice and since the accused had failed to make the payment in terms of the demand notice, he has committed the offence HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 5 of 21 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and hence is liable to be convicted for the same. 9.On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused that the present complaint is liable to be dismissed in view of the fact that the complainant has suppressed the material facts while filing the present complaint against the accused. According to him, the complainant has concealed the fact that the accused had availed two loans from the Centurion Bank of Punjab, out of which one was for a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/­ approx. and the another was for a sum of Rs. 50,000/­ approx. It is further submitted by him that the cheque Ex. Cw­1/2 was given by the accused to Centurion Bank of Punjab alongwith many other cheques as blank signed security cheque at the time of availing the first loan, which had already been repaid by him at the time of taking the top­up loan of Rs. 50,000/­. It is further submitted by him that AR of the complainant has admitted in his cross examination that his knowledge about the facts of the case was based on official records and he was unaware of the fact whether any blank cheques including the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 were taken by the complainant at the time of disbursal of loan. He also pleaded ignorance about the date and time of handing over of the aforesaid cheque to the complainant and further admitted that the cheque HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 6 of 21 was not handed over by the accused in his presence. Thus according to him the deposition of AR of the complainant regarding issuance of cheque in discharge of liability towards the loan taken by the accused is merely a piece of hearsay evidence in view of admission by him that the cheque was not handed over by the accused to the complainant in his presence. It is therefore submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused that the accused has examined himself on oath on this aspect and categorically deposed that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 is one out of six­seven blank signed cheques issued as security in favour of Centurion Bank of Punjab at the time of availing first loan from the later. According to him, these facts coupled with the fact that the cheque bears the name of Centurion Bank of Punjab as payee, instead of the name of the complainant bank, despite the fact that the former bank had already been merged with the complainant bank prior to the date mentioned in the cheque clearly shows that the stand taken by the accused that the cheque was issued as security in favour of the former bank is more probable than the case of complainant that the cheque was issued in discharge of liability by the accused in favour of the complainant bank. CW­1 has failed to justify his denial of suggestion to the effect that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was given by the accused to Centurion Bank of Punjab at the time of disbursal of HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 7 of 21 the first loan in favour of the accused. Thus according to Ld. Counsel for the accused, the cheque having been issued as security for some other loan and not for payment of any debt or liability, the complaint under Section 138 of the NI Act is not maintainable in view of Judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Collage Culture and Ors. v. Apparel Export Promotion Council and Anr. Even otherwise, according to Ld. Counsel for the accused, although the complainant has alleged that the accused had availed a top­up loan of Rs. 1,58,000/­ which was repayable in 60 EMIs of Rs. 4,510/­ each but it has utterly failed to prove either the disbursal of the aforesaid loan to the accused or the exact liability of the accused as on the date mentioned in the cheque. According to Ld. Counsel for the accused, the signatures of the accused on Ex. CW­1/Y were taken by the complainant on blank proformas and independent of the aforesaid document, no evidence has been led by the complainant to prove the alleged disbursal to the tune of Rs. 1,58,000/­ or for that matter of Rs. 1,46,000/­. Moreover according to him, the complainant has not proved the alleged statement of account of the accused which is Ex. CW­ 1/X as per the provisions of Bankers Books Evidence Act and the same has not been admitted by the accused. It is further submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused that the complainant has also failed to prove the HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 8 of 21 service of legal notice on the accused. 10.On the basis of aforesaid submissions made on behalf of both the parties, the following issues arise for determination. a) Whether the Cheque Ex. CW­1/2 has been issued by the accused in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability so as to attract the provisions of Section 138 of the NI Act? b) Whether the legal notice in terms of Proviso (b) to Section 138 of the NI Act has been served upon the accused or not? I shall deal with the aforesaid issues one by one. a) Whether the Cheque Ex. Cw­1/2 has been issued by the accused in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability so as to attract the provisions of Section 138 of the NI Act? 11. So far as the first issue is concerned, the case of the Complainant is that the accused had issued the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 in partial discharge of his outstanding liabilities towards the top up loan taken by him from the erstwhile Centurion bank of Punjab, as reflected in the statement of loan account Ex. CW­1/X. On the other hand, the case of accused is that the cheque alongwith some other cheques, was given to the erstwhile HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 9 of 21 Centurion Bank of Punjab as blank signed security cheque at the time of disbursal of the first loan and not for alleged repayment of the top­up loan and the same has been misused by the Complainant bank without any consent or information of the accused. According to Ld. Counsel for the accused, the accused has sufficiently rebutted the presumption under Section 139 of the NI Act, arising in favour of the complainant that the cheque was issued in discharge of any debt or liability. According to Ld. Counsel for the accused, while the complainant has failed to prove that the cheque was issued in discharge of the aforesaid liability the accused has stepped into the witness box and has categorically deposed that the cheque was given by him as blank signed security cheque at the time of disbursal of the first loan. According to Ld. Counsel for the accused the aforesaid testimony of the accused is further corroborated by the fact that the cheque has been issued in the name of M/s Centurion Bank of Punjab although as on the date mentioned in the cheque, the Centurion Bank of Punjab had already been merged with the complainant bank. According to him, if it were true that the cheque was given by the accused to the complainant as on the date mentioned in the cheque, it would have been issued in the name of complainant as according to the complainant the former bank had already been merged with the complainant as on HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 10 of 21 20.05.2008 i.e. much prior to 23.05.2009, the date mentioned in the cheque. It would be pertinent at this stage to reproduce the relevant provisions of Section 138 , 139 and Section 118 of the NI Act. Section 138 of the NI Act reads as under: "138. Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account. ­ Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provision of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both : Provided that nothing contained in this section shall apply unless ­ (a) the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier; (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 11 of 21 unpaid; and (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. Explanation :­ For the purposes of this section, `debt or other liability' means a legally enforceable debt or other liability." Section 139 of the NI Act reads as under: 139. Presumption in favour of holder:­ It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in Section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability. Moreover, relevant portion of the Section 118 of the NI Act reads as under: 118. Presumption as to negotiable instruments­Until the contrary is proved,the following presumptions shall be made:­ (a) of consideration­that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, indorsed, negotiated or transferred, was accepted, indorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration." 12. Issue regarding the scope of presumptions u/s 118(a) and u/s 139 of HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 12 of 21 the NI Act has come up for consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a number of cases. It is no longer res­integra that in order to rebut the aforesaid presumption accused is not liable to step into the witness box and the aforesaid presumptions can be rebutted even by cross examination of the complainant's witnesses. Moreover, the standard of proof required from the accused is preponderance of probabilities and accused is not required to prove the defence beyond reasonable doubts. 13. In the present case, although AR of the complainant has deposed in his affidavit Ex. CW­1/A to the effect that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was issued by the accused in discharge of his liabilities in terms of loan agreement number 91354455 but during cross examination, he admitted that the cheque was not given by the accused to the complainant in his presence and that he was not aware as to when the cheque was given by the accused to the complainant. CW­1 further stated that he was deposing on the basis of knowledge derived from the official records and while in the first instance he pleaded ignorance as to whether the complainant had taken any blank cheques including the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 from the accused at the time of disbursement of loan, later on, he blatantly denied the aforesaid suggestion given on behalf of the accused. However he has failed to justify the aforesaid denial by placing on record any documents HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 13 of 21 in support of the same. It is true that once the signatures on a cheque are admitted by the accused there is a presumption in favour of the complainant that the cheque was issued in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability. However, as stated hereinabove the aforesaid presumption is rebuttable in nature and the same can be rebutted even by cross examination of the complainant's witness. Here despite repeated suggestions, AR of the complainant had failed to depose as to exact date and time when the cheque in question was handed over by the accused to the complainant. Moreover, the accused has stepped into the witness box and deposed to the effect that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was given by the accused to M/s Centurion Bank of Punjab at the time of availing the first loan, and not to the complainant, as blank signed security cheque. Now the next question which falls for consideration is what is the weight to be attached to the aforesaid testimony of the accused in the facts and circumstances of the present case. In this regard, it would be pertinent to note herein that the accused was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the complainant and during the cross examination the accused had not only given evasive but had also given false replies to many of the questions put by Ld. Counsel for the complainant to him. For example, the deposition of the accused to the effect that he had already paid the HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 14 of 21 first loan of Rs. 1,00,000/­ to the Centurion Bank of Punjab in 30 equal monthly installments of Rs. 4,500/­ each prior to disbursal of top up loan in his favour is apparently false, in view of the fact that as per his own testimony, the accused has stated that the first loan was taken by him from the Centurion Bank of Punjab in the year 2006/2007 and the top­up loan of Rs. 50,000/­ approx. was taken by him in the month of march 2007. Now, if we assume that the first loan was taken by the accused in January 2006 (in view of the fact that according to the accused the first loan was taken by him either in the year 2006 or 2007 although he did not remember the exact date or month of availing the aforesaid loan), by any stretch of imagination it is not possible to accept that 30 equal monthly installments could have been paid by the accused by March 2007, as by march 2007 only 15 months would have expired since the date of disbursal of the loan. Thus the aforesaid part of testimony of the accused is apparently false. But as has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in a number of cases, the maxim­ "falsus in uno, falsus in omnibus", is not applicable as a rule of evidence in criminal trials in India and it is only a rule of caution. It is well settled that in such cases it is the duty of the court to separate the grain from the chaff and truth from the falsehood. Thus, the court is required to analyze the testimony of the HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 15 of 21 accused more cautiously and if possible to look for independent corroboration before accepting any part of testimony of the accused. In the present case, the accused has taken a consistent stand that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was given by the accused to Centurion Bank of Punjab at the time of availing the first loan as blank signed security cheque and the complainant has failed to prove to the contrary by examining the person to whom the alleged cheque was handed over by the accused or else by production of any receipt which might have been issued by the complainant in favour of the accused in respect of the aforesaid cheque. Moreover, admittedly the cheque has been drawn in favour of Centurion Bank of Punjab and if it was given by the accused to the complainant on or around the date mentioned in the cheque, there was no reason for the accused to draw the cheque in favour of Centurion Bank of Punjab in view of the alleged merger of the later with the complainant bank. Thus, in my considered view, the accused has successfully rebutted the presumption arising in favour of the complainant under Section 139 of the NI Act and hence the first question is answered in the negative. b) Whether the legal notice in terms of Proviso (b) to Section 138 of the NI Act has been served upon the accused or not? HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 16 of 21 14. So far as the second issue is concerned, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the complainant has proved the service of legal notice in terms of proviso (b) to Section 138 of the NI Act on the accused by placing on record the office copy of legal notice, postal receipts regarding dispatch of the same to the correct address of the accused and acknowledgment cards regarding receipt of the same. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the accused submits that the complainant has failed to prove the service of notice on the accused and although the AD cards have been purportedly signed in the name of mother of the accused, but the accused has denied that the signatures on the AD cards are of his mother. I have considered the rival submissions made on behalf of both the parties and have perused the record in the light of legal principles. On a perusal of evidence adduced by both the parties it appears that CW­1 has categorically deposed in para 8 of his affidavit Ex. CW­1/A that the demand notice, copy of which is Ex. CW­1/4 was served upon the accused through registered AD and the original postal receipts alongwith the acknowledgment cards in respect of the same are Ex. CW­1/5 (Colly). The aforesaid testimony of the AR of the complainant had remained uncontroverted despite the fact that the witness was cross examined at length by Ld. counsel for the accused on three occasions. Moreover, it HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 17 of 21 has been admitted by the accused during his cross examination that the address mentioned in the legal notice was his correct address and once it is proved that the legal notice was sent to the accused at his correct address after pre­ payment of the postal charges, there is a presumption under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act and under section114 of the Evidence Act regarding delivery of the same to the addressee in due course. Although the aforesaid presumption is rebuttable in nature, however, the accused has failed to lead any evidence to rebut the same except to the extent of making a bald statement that he did not receive the legal notice. Moreover in view of the observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment reported as CC Alavi Haji V. Palapatty Muhammed & Another to the effect that "a person who does not pay within 15 days on receipt of the summons from the Court alongwith the copy of complaint u/s 138 of the NI Act cannot obviously contend that he was not properly served with the notice as required u/s 138 of the NI Act , by ignoring statutory presumption to the contrary u/s 27 of General Clauses Act and Section 114 of the Evidence Act", the aforesaid contention does not lie in the mouth of the accused at this stage that too in view of the fact that no suggestion as aforesaid has ever been given to the AR for the complainant during his cross examination to this effect. HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 18 of 21 Hence in view of the aforesaid discussion, the question is answered in affirmative as the complainant has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the legal notice has been served upon the accused. 15. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussions, although the complainant has proved that the legal notice in respect of dishonour of the Cheque Ex. Cw­1/2 has been duly served upon the accused but the accused has established that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was given by him to Centurion Bank of Punjab at the time of disbursal of first loan by the later in his favour as a blank signed security cheque and not in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability in respect of the top­up loan as alleged by the complainant. Ld. Counsel for the complainant further sought to argue that even if the cheque was issued as security, still the accused is liable to be convicted under Section 138 of the NI Act, once the cheque is dishonoured on presentation. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the accused submits that once it is proved that the cheque Ex. CW­1/2 was issued as security and not in discharge of any liability towards the top­up loan, Section 138 of the NI Act has no application to the facts of the present case. Ld. Counsel for the accused has relied upon the Delhi High Court judgment in Collage Culture's Case (supra) in support of his submissions. HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 19 of 21 16. I have considered the rival submissions made on behalf of both the parties and have also gone through the judgments relied upon by both the parties. In Collage Culture case (supra), after discussions as to when can a cheque be said to have been issued in discharge of a debt due and when it can be said to have been issued as security, the Hon'ble High Court has observed as follows: "24. It would be relevant to note that the statute does not refer to the debt being payable, meaning thereby, a post dated cheque for a debt due but payment postponed at a future date would attract Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881. But the cheque issued not for an existing due, but issued by way of a security, would not attract Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, for it has not been issued for a debt which has come into in existence." While coming to the aforesaid conclusion Hon'ble High Court had relied upon the following observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in M.S.Narayana Menon v. State of Kerala & Anr. (2006) 6 SCC 39: "52. ........If the defence is acceptable as probable the cheque therefore cannot be held to have been issued in discharge of the debt as, for example, if a cheque is issued for security or for any other purpose the same would not come within the purview of Section 138 of the Act." HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 20 of 21 17. In view of the aforesaid authoritative pronouncements, I fail to agree with the submissions made on behalf of the complainant as, in my considered opinion, once the defence regarding issuance of cheque by way of security is found to be acceptable, there is no escape from the conclusion that Section 138 of NI Act is not attracted in case of dishonour of such a cheque. 18. In view of aforesaid facts and circumstances, in my considered opinion, the Complainant has failed to prove its case under Section 138 of the NI Act against the accused beyond reasonable doubts. Therefore the accused is acquitted of charges under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881(as amended upto date). 19. Ordered accordingly. Pronounced in the Open Court on this 14th day of November 2011. This Judgment consists of 21 signed pages. (ARUN KUMAR) Metropolitan Magistrate:Dwarka Courts 14.11.2011 HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Manoj Bansal Judgment dated 14.11.2011 CC No. 11607/09 Page 21 of 21
